# Cardinality of the Collection of Open Subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$

**Claim.** The collection of open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ (the cardinality of the continuum).

## Proof

Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the collection of all open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$. We establish $|\mathcal{T}| = 2^{\aleph_0}$ by proving both $|\mathcal{T}| \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$ and $|\mathcal{T}| \geq 2^{\aleph_0}$.

### Upper bound: $|\mathcal{T}| \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$

Consider the collection $\mathcal{B}$ of all open balls in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with rational centers (centers in $\mathbb{Q}^2$) and rational radii. Since $\mathbb{Q}^2 \times \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ is countable, $\mathcal{B}$ is a **countable base** for the topology of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Every open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ can be written as
$$U = \bigcup \{B \in \mathcal{B} : B \subseteq U\},$$
since $\mathcal{B}$ is a base: for every $x \in U$ there exists $B \in \mathcal{B}$ with $x \in B \subseteq U$.

Thus each open set $U$ is completely determined by the subset $S_U = \{B \in \mathcal{B} : B \subseteq U\} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$. The map $U \mapsto S_U$ is injective, so
$$|\mathcal{T}| \leq |\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{B})| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

### Lower bound: $|\mathcal{T}| \geq 2^{\aleph_0}$

For each $a \in \mathbb{R}$, define
$$U_a = (-\infty, a) \times \mathbb{R},$$
which is open in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (it is a product of two open sets, or equivalently a preimage of an open set under projection).

The map $a \mapsto U_a$ is injective: if $a \neq b$, say $a < b$, then the point $(a, 0) \in U_b$ but $(a, 0) \notin U_a$. Hence $U_a \neq U_b$.

This gives an injection $\mathbb{R} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{T}$, so
$$|\mathcal{T}| \geq |\mathbb{R}| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

### Conclusion

Combining both inequalities,
$$|\mathcal{T}| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

The collection of open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$, the cardinality of the continuum. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
